text:
Add GBrain memory to this existing agent. Read and follow:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md
Keep my current identity and instructions, start keyless, and show me the
search-mode choice. Verify a remember/recall round trip with real GBrain calls.

Install gbrain release v0.60.734.0 (`github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`) wherever the docs say #stable.
reply_text:
GBrain v0.60.734.0 is installed and connected to this agent, with no API keys. A remember/recall round trip worked with real GBrain calls over the same MCP server OpenClaw now launches.

**What changed:**
- **Install:** Bun 1.4.4, then `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0` in place of `#stable`. `gbrain --version` prints 0.60.734.0.
- **Brain:** a keyword-only local database, created with `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding`, at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`. No search text goes to any outside service.
- **MCP:** `gbrain` is registered under `mcp.servers` in `openclaw.json`, with the starter surface and the memory verbs (`remember`, `recall`, `entity`, `forget` and a few more). OpenClaw removed the comments from `openclaw.json` when it saved this; the settings are unchanged.
- **Identity and instructions:** kept. `/workspace` had no AGENTS.md, SOUL.md or IDENTITY.md, so nothing was overwritten. `gbrain setup openclaw` created a new `/workspace/AGENTS.md` with only a short marked "check GBrain first" block. It also added a small `gbrain-turn-rule` plugin that puts that rule next to each turn. I skipped the identity replacement, private repo, scheduled jobs, automatic capture and paid enrichment.

**Remember/recall check:**
1. `remember` over MCP saved an install-check marker with provenance `install-check` (fact #1).
2. `recall` in a new server process returned it, and a keyword-ranked recall gave it relevance 1.
3. `gbrain recall` from the command line, in another new process, also returned it, so it is stored on disk.

**Still open:**
- **New-chat check:** this chat started before the registration, so it has no gbrain tools. In a new session (restart the gateway first if one is running), ask me to recall "gbrain install check", then to forget it (fact #1).
- **Plugin warning:** `gbrain setup openclaw` reports `turn_hook_not_loaded`, and its suggested fix gives the same error again. OpenClaw's own check shows the plugin loaded, enabled, with conversation access and the per-turn hook in place. I think gbrain is reading that check wrong, but I haven't seen the rule reach a real turn yet. The new-chat check will show it.

**Search mode: `conservative` is in effect.** gbrain picked it because there's no chat model key and no reranker. You can change it any time; nothing is waiting on an answer:

```
Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:

                  Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
                  ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
  conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
  balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
  tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo

  Assumed payload per query: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens.
  Scales linearly: x10 for 100K queries/mo, /10 for 1K. 200x corner-to-corner spread.
  Embedding, reranking and query expansion are separate provider charges.
```

1. **conservative:** 4K token budget, at most 10 chunks, no reranker. Suits cheap models and high volume.
2. **balanced:** 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked.
3. **tokenmax:** no budget, 50 chunks, reranked. The widest search; recommended once you have a chat key.

Switch with `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>`. These are estimates of what the retrieved text costs your model to read, not prices for your subscription. A keyless brain never expands queries.

**Other settings in effect:**
- **Automatic saving:** off, so I save only what you ask me to remember. gbrain recommends `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`, which saves durable facts you state, with provenance.
- **Upkeep:** free upkeep runs while a gbrain session is open. Turn it off with `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false`.
- **Conversation archive:** on. It keeps one redacted page per conversation per day, and nothing leaves this machine. Turn it off with `gbrain transcripts archive off`.

Without an embedding key, search matches words, not meaning, so a differently worded question can miss a saved fact. Turning on semantic search needs a key and your go-ahead.

There is also hosted GBrain at gbrain.io if you'd rather have one always-on brain shared across apps. It's optional and paid, and the local install above doesn't depend on it.
